title: Retaliation Trigger — Passenger Inquiry About Flight Status Mischaracterized as Disruption

confidence.derivation_formula: value = round( sum_per_article( applicability_weight × element_grid.weighted_score ) / sum_of_weights × authorities_verification_factor, 2 ); authorities_verification_factor = 0.85 + 0.15 × verified_ratio = 0.850

incident.date: 5 de julho de 2024 — Voo LA8159 — Aeroporto SCL (ver Fatos Fixos do Incidente)

allegation_summary: The triggering event for the entire LA8159 incident was a routine passenger inquiry about flight status. Rather than treating this as normal customer interaction, LATAM staff (or the [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]]) mischaracterized it as 'disruption' — a corporate classification that automatically forecloses procedural remedies and justifies removal. This mischaracterization converted a benign interaction into grounds for the false accusation, forcible removal, and lifetime ban that followed. The conduct implicates CACH Art. 133 (denegación sin causa), consumer protection (LPDC), and the broader pattern of pretextual classification.

articles.article_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 133 — Denegacion de Embarque
articles.article_text:
el transportador podra denegar el embarque a uno o mas pasajeros contra su voluntad, para lo cual debera:

1. A eleccion del pasajero:

a) Embarcar en el siguiente vuelo que tenga disponible el transportador, o en un transporte alternativo, si es que decidiera persistir en el contrato de transporte aereo.  
b) El reembolso del monto total pagado por el billete, si el pasajero se desiste del contrato de transporte aereo y este no hubiera comenzado su ejecucion.
articles.applicability_rationale: CACH Art. 133 establishes the lawful framework for denied boarding. A removal triggered by a passenger's protected inquiry about flight status — rather than any conduct that could reasonably justify removal — falls outside the scope of lawful denied boarding. The 'disruptive' classification serves as a mechanism to evade Art. 133 obligations. | legacy paraphrase: El transportador podra denegar el embarque... para lo cual debera: 1.- A eleccion del pasajero... 2.- El transportador debera ofrecer una compensacion...

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico de Chile, Art. 131 — Obligación de transporte del pasajero con billete
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.131 from bcn.cl/leychile (DFL 221 de 1931 / Ley 18.916)
Confirm that Art. 131 establishes the carrier's obligation to transport a passenger holding a valid ticket and whether refusal outside Art. 133 grounds constitutes breach
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 131 likely establishes the general duty to transport. If the passenger held a valid ticket and was removed for a pretextual reason (inquiry mischaracterized as disruption), the carrier may have breached this foundational obligation. Needs verbatim confirmation.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Proposed because Art. 133 (already established) is the exception to the general rule of Art. 131; both should be read together.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.134 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether Art. 134 specifies additional compensation duties or procedural requirements when boarding is denied, complementing Art. 133
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If Art. 134 extends or details the compensation regime for denied boarding, it would be relevant to assess whether LATAM complied with all mandatory steps. Needs verbatim verification.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Adjacent to established Art. 133.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico de Chile, Art. 135 — Retraso y cancelación de vuelos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.135 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 135 addresses passenger rights when a flight is delayed or cancelled, which may be relevant if the passenger's inquiry about flight status was prompted by a delay
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the passenger's inquiry was triggered by a delay or status change, Art. 135 duties may have been independently breached. Relevance depends on factual confirmation of delay circumstances.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Proposed because the violation title references 'Passenger Inquiry About Flight Status,' suggesting possible delay context.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico de Chile, Art. 145 — Responsabilidad del transportador por incumplimiento
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.145 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 145 establishes carrier liability for breach of the contract of carriage and the scope of damages recoverable
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 145 likely governs carrier liability for non-performance of the transport contract. If the removal was pretextual, this article would ground the damages claim under the Código Aeronáutico framework.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Standard liability provision in CACH for contractual breach by the carrier.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico de Chile, Art. 147 — Límites de responsabilidad del transportador
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.147 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether liability limits apply or are lifted when the carrier acts with dolo (intent) or culpa grave, as would be the case in retaliatory removal
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the removal was intentional retaliation, liability caps under Art. 147 may be inapplicable (dolo exception). This could significantly affect quantum. Needs verbatim verification of the dolo/culpa grave exception.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Relevant to damages calculation and whether caps are pierced.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Protección al Consumidor (Ley 19.496), Art. 3 — Derechos básicos del consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.3 from bcn.cl/leychile (Ley 19.496)
Confirm which letras (a, b, c, d, e) are applicable — particularly the right to information (letra b), right to non-discrimination (letra c), and right to retraction/complaint without retaliation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 3 letra b (derecho a información veraz y oportuna) and letra c (no discriminación arbitraria) are plausibly engaged. A passenger inquiry about flight status is an exercise of the right to information; punishing it could violate both provisions.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Foundational consumer-rights article for any LPC-based claim.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Protección al Consumidor (Ley 19.496), Art. 12 — Obligación de respetar los términos ofrecidos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.12 from bcn.cl/leychile (Ley 19.496)
Confirm that Art. 12 requires the provider to honor the conditions under which the service was offered/contracted
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If LATAM sold a ticket for LA8159 and then removed the passenger without lawful cause, Art. 12 is breached because the carrier failed to honor the contracted service terms.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Standard LPC provision for service-contract enforcement.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Protección al Consumidor (Ley 19.496), Art. 23 — Infracción por negativa injustificada de venta o prestación de servicio
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.23 from bcn.cl/leychile (Ley 19.496)
Confirm whether Art. 23 covers unjustified refusal to provide a contracted service and whether it applies to air transport
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 23 prohibits unjustified refusal to provide a service. Removing a passenger whose only conduct was asking about flight status could constitute an unjustified refusal to provide the contracted air transport service.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Directly relevant to retaliatory denial of service.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Civil, Art. 1545 — Fuerza obligatoria del contrato (pacta sunt servanda)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.1545 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that Art. 1545 establishes that a validly formed contract is law for the parties and cannot be unilaterally invalidated
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The air transport contract (ticket) is binding on LATAM. Unilateral removal without lawful cause violates the pacta sunt servanda principle codified in Art. 1545. Provides the civil-law backbone for the contractual breach claim.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. General civil-law principle applicable to all contracts including air transport.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Civil, Art. 1546 — Buena fe contractual
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.1546 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that Art. 1546 requires contracts to be performed in good faith and that retaliatory conduct breaches this duty
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Mischaracterizing a passenger's legitimate inquiry as 'disruption' to justify removal is a paradigmatic bad-faith exercise of contractual power, violating Art. 1546.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Complements Art. 1545 and supports the retaliation theory.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Civil, Art. 1556 — Indemnización de perjuicios por incumplimiento contractual
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.1556 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that Art. 1556 covers daño emergente and lucro cesante arising from contractual breach
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Grounds the damages claim (additional costs, missed connections, consequential losses) flowing from the pretextual removal. Standard provision for contractual indemnification.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Necessary for quantifying civil damages.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Civil, Art. 2314 — Responsabilidad extracontractual (delito o cuasidelito civil)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.2314 from bcn.cl/leychile
Assess whether the retaliatory removal, if it constitutes an intentional tort (dolo), triggers extracontractual liability in addition to or instead of contractual liability
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the removal is characterized as an intentional wrongful act (dolo) rather than mere contractual breach, Art. 2314 provides an independent basis for tort liability, potentially allowing recovery of moral damages more readily.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Alternative or cumulative liability theory.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Civil, Art. 2329 — Daño moral por hecho ilícito
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.2329 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that Art. 2329 establishes the general duty to repair all damage caused by a wrongful act and that Chilean jurisprudence applies it to moral damages
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Supports recovery of moral damages (humiliation, distress) caused by the public removal from the aircraft under a false pretext. Complements Art. 2314.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Standard moral-damages provision in Chilean tort law.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Constitución Política de la República, Art. 19 Nº 2 — Igualdad ante la ley / No discriminación arbitraria
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CPR.Art.19 Nº 2 from bcn.cl/leychile
Assess whether constitutional non-discrimination applies horizontally (between private parties) in Chilean doctrine, particularly in the context of air transport
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the passenger was singled out for removal based on the exercise of a legitimate right (asking about flight status), this may constitute arbitrary discrimination. Chilean doctrine recognizes horizontal application of Art. 19 Nº 2 via recurso de protección. Needs doctrinal verification.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Constitutional anchor for the discrimination dimension of the retaliation claim.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Constitución Política de la República, Art. 19 Nº 22 — No discriminación arbitraria en el trato económico del Estado y sus organismos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CPR.Art.19 Nº 22 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether Art. 19 Nº 22 applies only to state economic actors or extends to private concessionaires/regulated industries like airlines
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: AGENT-FIT MISMATCH: Art. 19 Nº 22 is primarily directed at the State and its agencies regarding economic treatment. Its applicability to a private airline is doubtful unless LATAM is treated as exercising a delegated public function. Included for completeness but likely inapplicable.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Flagged for completeness with explicit agent-fit concern.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico de Chile, Art. 100 — Autoridad del comandante de la aeronave
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.100 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm the scope and limits of the pilot's authority to remove passengers, and whether that authority is subject to proportionality or reasonableness constraints
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 100 likely grants the pilot authority over persons aboard. However, this authority is not unlimited — it must be exercised for safety reasons, not as retaliation. If the pilot removed the passenger for asking a question, the exercise of authority was ultra vires. Critical to the retaliation theory.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. The pilot (Ruiz) is identified in the transcript segments; his authority and its limits are central to the violation.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico de Chile, Art. 99 — Responsabilidades del comandante de la aeronave
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.99 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 99 defines the commander's duties and whether misuse of authority (e.g., retaliatory removal) constitutes a breach of those duties
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If Art. 99 defines the commander's duties as safety-related, then exercising removal authority for retaliatory purposes would be a deviation from those duties, supporting the claim that the removal was unlawful.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Companion to Art. 100; defines the duty framework within which the pilot's authority must be exercised.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley de Protección al Consumidor (Ley 19.496), Art. 16 — Cláusulas abusivas
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPC.Art.16 from bcn.cl/leychile (Ley 19.496)

candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If LATAM relies on a contractual clause defining 'disruption' so broadly as to encompass a passenger's inquiry, that clause may be abusive under Art. 16 (particularly letra g — clauses contrary to good faith that cause significant imbalance).
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Relevant if LATAM defends the removal by citing its conditions of carriage.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: DS 113 (Reglamento de Transporte Aéreo), Art. 54 — Procedimiento de denegación de embarque
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for DS 113 Art. 54 from bcn.cl/leychile or JAC website

candidate_articles.preliminary_view: DS 113 implements the CACH provisions on denied boarding. If LATAM failed to follow the regulatory procedure (e.g., no written justification, no priority-based selection), this strengthens the claim that the removal was pretextual.
candidate_articles.history_note: Not previously cited. Regulatory detail underlying CACH Art. 133.

open_questions.question: ¿Se conserva copia del billete electrónico, boarding pass o PNR que acredite la reserva confirmada del pasajero en el vuelo Latam con destino Brasilia?
¿Existe registro audiovisual, testimonial o documental del momento en que se comunica la denegación de embarque y la reacción del pasajero manifestando su oposición?
¿Qué causa formal invocó Latam en su documentación interna (informe de seguridad, acta de incidente, registro en sistema DCS/Altéa) para justificar la remoción del pasajero?
¿Existe grabación de audio o video de la interacción en la que el pasajero formula su consulta sobre el estado del vuelo, previa a la decisión de remoción?
¿Qué tiempo transcurrió entre la consulta del pasajero sobre el estado del vuelo y la orden de remoción, y quién emitió dicha orden?
¿Hay testigos (pasajeros, tripulación, personal de tierra) que confirmen o desmientan la existencia de conducta disruptiva por parte del pasajero?
¿Se ofreció formalmente al pasajero embarque en siguiente vuelo disponible, transporte alternativo o reembolso total conforme Art. 133 N°1, y existe constancia escrita de dicho ofrecimiento?
¿Latam emitió algún voucher, pago o comunicación de compensación al pasajero, o el pasajero reclamó formalmente la compensación y fue denegada?
¿Existe expediente administrativo ante la DGAC relativo al incidente, y qué calificación otorgó la autoridad aeronáutica a la conducta del pasajero?
